The fixed HTTPS URL with userinfo on the real allowed provider CDN is a hostile input. The test requires rejection before fetching; it is not an email address or credential. Changing the host would test host rejection instead of userinfo rejection.

These exact malformed mailbox fixtures exercise one-character and numeric-only top-level domain rejection before any provider write. Replacing them with valid reserved domains would remove the boundary cases. All values are synthetic test inputs.

Verified PNG compressed-data false positive: one six-byte match at file offset 39208 lies wholly in an IDAT payload. All chunk CRCs and the complete zlib raster stream validate. The bytes are absent from inflated scanlines and non-IDAT payloads; the image has no textual metadata chunks. Original browser-capture pixels and bytes are retained.
